content:
jordan: Quick escalation — QuantiumPay (dedicated pool qp-42 in us-west2) reports sustained 429s this morning during their billing-run window. They say TPS spiked from 120 -> 900 and our admission control started rejecting requests.

samir: Saw the alert, digging in. Do we have burst credits for qp-42?

ops-bot: [alert] qp-42: token-per-second headroom exhausted, admission_control triggered (policy=strict), 429 rate 36% in last 5m.

eva: Customer says autoscaler didn't add nodes fast enough; they saw a 3m window where 429s spiked. They're pointing to our SLO for tokens/sec.

samir: Pulling perf logs + allocator metrics. Initial findings: burst_credits for qp-42 were at 0 at 09:12:03 UTC. Autoscaler policy is target_util=0.6, cooldown=120s, max_scale_step=1. For the spike we saw the following:

```
09:11:58 incoming_tps=920
09:12:00 burst_credits=0
09:12:01 admission_control=reject
09:12:04 GPU_util=98% (node-7)
09:12:12 scale_event=start node-8 (requested)
09:12:45 node-8 ready
09:12:50 admission_control=accept
```

samir: So autoscaler requested 1 node but the new pod/container took ~40s to be ready (image pull + warmup). That gap correlates with the 3m window.

maria: Is there evidence of noisy neighbor? Customer mentioned a single tenant on the pool was running long llama-chat sessions concurrently.

samir: I checked per-tenant GPU kernel times — one tenant (internal integration test) had an elevated per-token latency and long KV cache retention causing GPU memory spikes. That contributed to node saturation.

jordan: Any immediate mitigation we can push while we triage? Customer is affected and billing-run is time-sensitive.

eva: Short term: 1) bump qp-42 to allow emergency burst credits (if org allows), 2) temporarily loosen admission_control to permissive for this pool, 3) if allowed, manually provision an extra node to avoid wait for autoscaler. Which has least blast radius?

samir: Order of safety: manual add node, grant emergency burst (but doesn't help if credits are already 0), adjust admission_control policy (risky — could cause degradation). I'd do manual add node + pull logs for noisy job and throttle it.

jordan: I'm going to open ticket with QuantiumPay and propose manual node + throttling noisy tenant. Eva will coordinate.

eva: On it. Contacted customer: "we can add capacity now — allow up to 2 extra nodes, or we can pause the internal integration tests for 20 minutes." They asked for us to add capacity.

ops-bot: [action] manual_scale qp-42 +2 nodes initiated by eva at 09:13:05 UTC.

samir: Added a temporary admission rule to prioritize dedicated-customer traffic over internal integration tests. Applied a cpu/gpu quota for integration job jid=integ-333.

```
kubectl patch hpa qp-42-hpa -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":10}}'
# applied temporary QoS: evict-integ label -> best-effort
```

maria: Customer reports 429s dropping to near 0 after 90s of the scale action. They see throughput back to ~640 tps.

jordan: Good. Notes for postmortem: autoscaler warmup + image pull latency + noisy neighbor = admission control triggered + burst credits exhausted. Need runbook items.

samir: Suggested follow-ups:
- Pre-warm images for scheduled heavy windows (cron hook).
- Increase burst_credit cap or soft warm-headroom for known billing windows.
- Reduce autoscaler cooldown or increase max_scale_step for high-risk pools.
- Add per-tenant throttles / QoS to avoid noisy internal jobs.
- Improve metrics to emit "estimated_ready_seconds" when scale requested.

eva: I'll collect repro steps and a minimal log bundle for the eng-runtime team. Repro: simulate 3x traffic for 2m with empty burst credits and see admission behavior.

samir: Experiment notes to add to ticket: run JMeter loop with header X-Tokens-Per-Second target=900, set pool qp-42 burst_credits=0, simulate image-pull delay by adding 20s to node join, observe 429 window.

jordan: Creating support ticket: https://support.redwood.example/tickets/REND-91234 (customer-visible). Also creating internal incident for runtime team: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-8341.

maria: Action items assigned:
- samir: perf logs + kernel traces (due EOD)
- eva: customer comms + temporary node scaling audit (10m)
- jordan: postmortem draft + headroom planning proposal (by tomorrow)

ops-bot: [note] incident INC-8341 created and assigned to eng-runtime.

jordan: Thanks team. We'll follow up with a short runbook patch for dedicated pools that have scheduled high TPS windows. :thumbsup:
